{{nihongo|'''Suhama Shrine (Daito, Osaka)'''|須波麻神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Suhama Shrine''' (すはまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Nakagaito, {{ill|Daitō, Osaka|ar|دايتو (أوساكا)|arz|دايتو|ca|Daitō|ce|Дайто (гӀала)|ceb|Daitō Shi|cv|Дайто (хула)|de|Daitō (Osaka)|eo|Dajto|es|Daitō (Osaka)|et|Daitō|fa|دایتو، اوساکا|fi|Daitō|fr|Daitō (Osaka)|gl|Daitō|id|Daitō, Ōsaka|it|Daitō|ja|大東市|ko|다이토시|mg|Daitōchō|mzn|دایتو، اوساکا|nl|Daito|no|Daitō|pl|Daitō (miasto)|pt|Daito|ro|Daitō|ru|Дайто (город)|sh|Daito|simple|Daitō, Osaka|sr|Даито|sv|Daito|tg|Дайто|th|ไดโต|tl|Daitō, Osaka|tr|Daitō, Osaka|tt|Дайто (шәһәр)|uk|Дайто|ur|ڈائٹو، اوساکا|vi|Daitō, Ōsaka|war|Daitō, Osaka|zh|大東市|zh_classical|大東市|zh_min_nan|Daitô-chhī|zh_yue|大東市|qid=Q386668}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
[[File:Kurogane-mochi at Suhama Shrine.jpg|Thumbnail|The {{ill|Ilex rotunda|arz|اليكس روتوندا|ceb|Ilex rotunda|et|Ümar iileks|fa|خاس کوروگانه|ja|クロガネモチ|ko|먼나무|sv|Ilex rotunda|uk|Ilex rotunda|vi|Ilex rotunda|war|Ilex rotunda|zh|鐵冬青|zh_yue|鐵冬青|qid=Q844306}} tree (a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=protected tree}}) within the shrine grounds]]
According to tradition, the shrine was once considered identical in essence to {{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}} and held its grand festival on October 7. Although the details of its founding are unclear, it is already listed in the Heian-period “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},” and it is the only {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} within Daitō City. From {{ill|Sasara district|ja|讃良郡|zh|讚良郡|qid=Q11632569}} to {{ill|Wakae district|Q11616589|qid=Q11616589}}, it once had parishioners from several dozen villages. In 1873 (Meiji 6), it became the {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} for eleven villages within Sanra District, and in September 1907 (Meiji 40), three shrines—{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtani Shrine}} in Teragawa, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ryūma Shrine}} in Ryūma, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Zama Shrine}} in Fukano—were temporarily merged into it. Today, it serves as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} (local tutelary deity) of Nakagaito.

;About the shrine name
In ancient times, the area where this shrine stands was part of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Bay}}, which later became {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawachi Lagoon}}, then {{ill|Kawachi Bay|Q11553429|qid=Q11553429}}, gradually shrinking due to sediment inflow from rivers such as the {{ill|Yodo River|Q1140505|qid=Q1140505}} and the {{ill|Yamato River|Q9001527|qid=Q9001527}}. As this happened, settlements were gradually established, though large ponds such as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fukakai Pond}} and {{ill|Fukano Pond|Q11560330|qid=Q11560330}} remained. It is said that the western side of this shrine once bordered such waters, and there is a theory that the shrine originally enshrined not {{ill|Ōkuninushi|abstract|Q276944|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}} but a different water deity to ward off water-related disasters. The current name is thought to derive from “Nagisahama / Suhama” (meaning shoreline or waterside). Incidentally, the place name “Suhama” is the oldest known place name in Daitō City.

=== Shrine grounds ===
[[File:Stone lanterns at Suhama Shrine (guidepost).jpg|Thumbnail|[[Lantern|Stone lantern]] (also serving as a {{ill|signpost|Q22812402|qid=Q22812402}})]]
In front of the shrine buildings stands a large naturally growing kurogane-mochi tree, designated as a protected tree by Daitō City.

There are a total of eleven stone lanterns on the grounds. Among them, the lantern placed at the entrance, made in 1830 (Bunsei 13), also served as a guidepost and was relocated from the nearby {{ill|Higashi Kōya Kaidō|Q11528777|qid=Q11528777}} route.
